entities.name: Pronation ankle sprain
observations: Pain with passive dorsiflexion, eversion, and abduction reproduces pronation and most directly indicates a pronation-pattern ankle sprain.
The mechanism may stress the medial ankle restraints, especially the deltoid ligament complex, and possibly the syndesmosis when external rotation or proximal syndesmotic tenderness is present.

entities.name: Syndesmotic ankle sprain
observations: An isolated syndesmotic sprain is more characteristically associated with external rotation and dorsiflexion, distal tibiofibular ligament pain, and positive squeeze or external-rotation tests.
The described pronation maneuver alone does not make syndesmotic sprain the primary diagnosis.

entities.name: Deltoid ligament strain
observations: A forceful eversion/abduction mechanism can injure the deltoid ligament, but the listed clinical motion pattern identifies a broader pronation mechanism rather than an isolated deltoid injury.
